title: eludite.debug.trace input
description: Instrument and run in one call: install tracepoints at `points` (each prints its `message` and continues; Visual Studio's "When Hit... Print a message and Continue"), resume the debuggee (or start it, `run: start`), collect the lines they print in order until `until` holds, then remove the points (a line's existing breakpoint is restored). Prefer it to breakpoints and single steps when the question is "what values pass through here": no stop is shown and nothing waits for a call per hit. Where the debug adapter has no log points (netcoredbg) each hit costs a stop and a resume in the debugger (`overhead_ms_per_hit` says how much); `max_hits` caps the cost. `message` takes `{expression}` (evaluated in the hit frame: it runs debuggee code), `$FUNCTION`, `$CALLER`, `$TID` and `$TNAME`. Needs break mode (`run: continue`) or no session (`run: start`). The lines also go to the Output window's Debug source and the `debug` output (eludite.debug.output). Next: read `lines`; `stopped_by: stopped` comes with the stop summary.
x-eludite-escalates: Dangerous when the solution's policy sets `debug.drive` to `prompt`, or `debug.evaluate` to `prompt` and a point's message has an `{expression}`; refused for agents when `debug.drive` is `deny`, or `debug.evaluate` is `deny` and a message has an expression.

path.description: The source file (absolute or relative to the solution folder).

message.description: What to print at each hit: text with `{expression}` segments (evaluated in the hit frame; an error is written in place as `{expression: <error>}`; `{{` and `}}` are literal braces), `$FUNCTION`, `$CALLER`, `$TID` and `$TNAME`.

condition.description: Print only when this C# expression is true.

run.description: `continue` (default): resume the debuggee from break mode. `start`: start debugging first (no session may run), with `project`, `profile` and `build` as eludite.debug.start takes them.

project.description: The project to run: its path (absolute or relative to the solution folder) or its name as the Workspace window shows it. Default: the startup project (eludite.workspace.set_startup_project), else the solution's first executable project.

profile.description: The launchSettings.json profile to use. Default: the first profile whose commandName is Project.

build.description: Build the project before launching. Default: the setting build.beforeRun (true unless changed).

until.description: When to stop collecting: `terminated` (default: the session ends), `stopped` (the next visible stop: a breakpoint, an exception; the answer has its stop summary) or `hits` (the points were hit `count` times in all; the debuggee goes on running). Whatever `until` says, a visible stop (the debuggee in break mode) ends collecting with `stopped_by: stopped`, since nothing prints until someone resumes it.

count.description: With `until: hits`: how many hits (1 to 10000).

wait_ms.description: How long to collect at most, in milliseconds (default 10000, at most 30000); then `stopped_by` is `timeout` and the debuggee goes on running.

max_hits.description: The most lines collected (default 1000, at most 10000). Reaching it disables the points (the debuggee keeps running) and sets `truncated`.

stop.description: The stop the caller saw (`stop` in eludite.debug.state). When given and the debuggee has stopped or resumed since, the command is refused as stale instead of acting on a state the caller did not see (two drivers, PLAN.md 5.5).

depth.description: How many levels of the locals to expand: 1 (default) lists the top level only; up to 5. Expansion is breadth-first and stops when `max_variables` rows are listed.

max_variables.description: The most variable rows listed, counting every level (default 50, at most 500).

max_value_chars.description: Values longer than this are cut and end with `… (N chars)`, the row saying `value_truncated` (default 200, at most 10000).

max_frames.description: The most stack frames listed (default 10, at most 200); page further with eludite.debug.stack.

max_output_lines.description: The most program output lines listed (default 20, at most 1000; 0 lists none).

output_since.description: An output cursor (`output.next` of an earlier answer, or eludite.debug.output's `next`): list the program's lines from it on. Default: the last `max_output_lines` lines.
